title: Heuristic tiered trace sampler and emit throttler to reduce per-request tracing overhead
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: As request QPS grows, our distributed tracing library is adding measurable CPU and memory pressure on hot path services. Existing tail/adaptive samplers reduce storage but still carry steady per-request cost (span allocation, tag collection, and periodic emission). Goal: introduce a lightweight, heuristic tiered sampler plus an emit throttler to lower per-request overhead while preserving signal for SLO regressions and incidents.
motivation_goals: 1) Cut per-request tracing CPU by ~40-60% on p95/p99 traffic paths. 2) Maintain high-fidelity traces for errors and latency regressions. 3) Provide graceful degradation under burst traffic with bounded trace emission budgets.
solution_outline:
- Tiered heuristic sampler evaluated at ingress: classify requests into "critical", "high-prob" and "background" sampling tiers using cheap signals (endpoint type, request headers, response code hints, raw latency so far, token-count estimate).
- Critical: always sample full trace (errors, admin routes, synthetic traffic markers).
- High-prob: sample with elevated probability (e.g., 25-50%) for endpoints known to be flaky or high-business-value.
- Background: apply aggressive probabilistic sampling plus lightweight span placeholder (no attribute copies) for very high QPS routes.
- Emit throttler: a global per-service budget that enforces a maximum traces/sec and prioritizes critical over high-prob over background. Budgets are refilled periodically and decay with burst control.
- Micro-optimizations: avoid allocation of span attribute maps for unsampled traces, move JSON serialization off main request thread, replace coarse locks in aggregator with sharded atomics, add a thin prefilter to short-circuit trace creation for known low-value callers.
tradeoffs_considered:
- Heuristic tiers are lossy vs. full tail-sampling (may miss some rare anomalies) but reduce steady overhead.
- Complexity: introduces more config knobs (tiers, budgets) vs. single adaptive algorithm; mitigated by sane defaults and telemetry.
- Observability vs. cost: we prioritize error/latency signal; non-critical traces can be reconstructed via metrics and sampled logs if needed.
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end p95 CPU for tracer-enabled service reduced by >=40% on benchmark workload.
- Traces/sec emitted under synthetic burst limited to configured budget and prioritized correctly.
- No increase in tail latency >5ms introduced by sampler path.
- Dashboards updated showing sampling rates by tier and budget usage.
- Runtime flag to disable sampler without restart.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: RFC drafted and reviewed with Observability and Runtime teams. Link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Heuristic+Tiered+Sampler+RFC
2026-02-19: Prototype implemented in platform/tracing: lightweight ingress classifier and tier labels. Benchmarks show ~28% CPU reduction on small services.

2026-02-25: Sharded budget allocator implemented; discovered contention with global mutex — replaced with per-shard atomics.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4532

2026-03-03: Added emit throttler policy and background serializer worker. End-to-end benchmark: p95 tracer CPU down 46% on chat-router workload.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4567
2026-03-10: Integration tests failing intermittently under high-concurrency; root cause appears to be race when moving spans to background queue. Added jitter and backpressure; tests stabilizing.
review_feedback: PM (Jared Morales): ensure we surface a per-route override in Console before rollout to Dedicated customers.
Security (S. Patel): recommend threat model review for synthetic markers used to force-critical sampling; added ticket for review.
Runtime lead (Elena Park): prefer conservative defaults and a runtime-opt-out flag to speed rollback if regressions appear.
implementation_notes:
- Prefilter hook lives in tracer.ingress.hook and returns a tier enum; kept intentionally minimal to avoid heap allocations.
- Background worker batch size tuned to minimize latency impact while achieving throughput; default 128 spans/batch.
- Config exposed via remote flags with sensible cluster defaults and per-service overrides in Console.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for classifier heuristics and budget refills.
- Load tests (k6) reproducing p95/p99 traffic patterns with and without sampler.
- Chaos test that toggles budgets to validate graceful degradation.
- Canary rollout to non-critical namespace for 48 hours before org-wide rollouts.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature gated rollout behind runtime flag.
2) Canary to internal staging + two self-serve tenants for 48 hours.
3) Incremental enabling by traffic tier via Console (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
4) Post-rollout: 7-day monitor window for regressions and alert thresholds tied to sampler CPU and emitted traces/sec.
post_rollout_followups: Add UI in Console to visualize sampling tier distribution per-route.
Create migration tool to backfill missing metadata for traces dropped by background tier if customers request deeper analysis.
Evaluate combining with adaptive tail-sampler as a hybrid model in future iteration.
qa_notes:
Watch for flakiness in integration tests that assert exact emitted trace counts — tests should be updated to allow budget-driven variability.
Monitor for increased GC due to background queue resizing.
